name: Gold Scholarship (Gold Scholars Program)
value: Georgia residents: Tuition, Fees, and Books scholarship (valued about $12,500 annually). Out-of-state students: Tuition Waiver (valued about $21,000 annually; reduces cost to the in-state rate). Up to eight semesters of funding, plus retreats, mentoring and first-year housing priority.
deadline: Early Action 1: application October 15, 2026, documents October 30, 2026, self-reported test scores November 16, 2026. Early Action 2: application November 2, 2026, documents November 16, 2026, test scores December 8, 2026. All admission deadlines are 11:59 p.m. in the applicant's time zone. The Gold program calendar instead lists November 3, 2026 for EA2. Semifinalist interviews are in early February 2027; required finalist weekend April 9-10, 2027.
apply: Apply through the Common Application by the appropriate Early Action deadline; no separate initial scholarship application. Complete the transcript, SAT/ACT and requested admission documents. Selected semifinalists must complete an asynchronous virtual interview; finalists must attend all Stamps Scholars Weekend activities to remain eligible.
eligibility: First-year applicants (not transfers) who are citizens or permanent residents of the United States or the United Kingdom; citizens of the Republic of Ireland may also be considered. Offered to roughly the top two percent of the first-year class.
notes: The Georgia-resident package assumes a separately awarded Zell Miller Scholarship. Applicants must retain their primary application major through May 2028 for fall 2027 entry. General institutional aid renewal requires full-time enrollment, academic progress and good standing; Gold-specific GPA requirements are not published on the pages reviewed.

name: College of Engineering Dean's Scholars Program
value: $10,000 each academic year for up to 8 semesters, plus $2,000 for academic enrichment
deadline: Early Action 1: application October 15, 2026, documents October 30, 2026, self-reported test scores November 16, 2026. Early Action 2: application November 2, 2026, documents November 16, 2026, test scores December 8, 2026. All admission deadlines are 11:59 p.m. in the applicant's time zone. No separate scholarship application deadline is published.
apply: Apply for first-year admission through the appropriate Early Action plan for academic merit scholarship consideration. A reading committee and program administrators select 7 to 20 incoming engineering students each fall; no separate Dean's Scholars application is described.
eligibility: Incoming first-year undergraduates admitted to College of Engineering majors with exemplary academic achievement in high school and strong community service experience.
notes: Renewal requires a 3.0 GPA and completion of two courses in the Ivan Allen College of Liberal Arts or College of Design that complement the engineering major. Scholars participate in service learning, intellectual enrichment, philanthropy and program activities. Cohort size depends on donor funding.

name: Scheller College of Business Dean's Scholarship (incoming first-year)
value: Four-year scholarships ranging from $20,000 up to $50,000 during an undergraduate career; about 15 to 18 awarded each year
deadline: Early Action 1: application October 15, 2026, documents October 30, 2026, self-reported test scores November 16, 2026. Early Action 2: application November 2, 2026, documents November 16, 2026, test scores December 8, 2026. All admission deadlines are 11:59 p.m. in the applicant's time zone.
apply: Apply for first-year admission as a Business Administration student through the appropriate Early Action plan; no separate scholarship application is required. Complete admission transcripts, SAT/ACT and requested documents.
eligibility: High school students applying to enter the Georgia Tech summer or fall first-year class as Business Administration students, selected for academic performance, leadership, involvement and potential for success.
notes: Retain the Business Administration major, earn a 3.0 GPA at the end of first spring and 3.2 each subsequent semester, complete at least two core business courses in year one and four in each of years two and three, and participate in two to three required annual events and donor updates. Funding is limited to eight semesters within five calendar years, subject to good conduct, aid policy and cost-of-attendance limits. Disenrollment ends renewal unless preauthorized. Georgia residents may receive this award alongside HOPE or Zell Miller.

name: Dickinson Merit Scholarships and Academic Awards
value: $15,000 to $45,000 per year, renewable for eight semesters
deadline: Automatic merit consideration with the admission application. For fall 2027 admission: Early Decision I and Early Action November 15, 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 15, 2027.
apply: No additional application materials required; the admissions committee awards merit scholarships during application review.
eligibility: Admitted first-year students with exemplary academic performance and potential contribution to the college, without regard to financial need.
notes: General merit awards require full-time enrollment and a 2.0 GPA and cover eight semesters in residence or Dickinson study abroad. A separately published John Dickinson Scholarship page gives $20,000 per year and a 3.0 renewal GPA; follow the conditions on the individual award letter.

name: Reynolds Leadership Scholar Program
value: $50,000 per year toward tuition, $200,000 over eight semesters, plus leadership programming and mentoring
deadline: Submit both the admission application and Reynolds Scholarship application for fall 2027: November 15, 2026 for Early Decision I or Early Action; January 15, 2027 for Early Decision II or Regular Decision.
apply: Submit a Common Application or Coalition Application plus the separate Reynolds Scholarship form. Choose one brief essay prompt about entrepreneurial pursuits or leadership and community impact. The form confirms fall 2027 entry, though its application-plan selector omits Early Action despite listing its deadline.
eligibility: Maryland residents and/or students currently enrolled in a Maryland high school who show outstanding leadership, academic excellence and community impact.
notes: Keep with a 2.0 GPA and full-time enrollment.

name: Dickinson-Sandia Scholarship
value: Two full-tuition scholarships, for eight semesters of full-time study
deadline: Submit the complete admission application, FAFSA and CSS Profile by the admission deadline. For fall 2027 admission: Early Decision I and Early Action November 15, 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 15, 2027.
apply: No separate application. Submit a complete admission application plus the FAFSA and CSS Profile by the deadline; Early Decision applicants get preference.
eligibility: Incoming students who live or attend school in Arizona, New Mexico or Southern California (Imperial, Kern, Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Diego, Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo and Ventura counties) with community-service or community-leadership experience.
notes: Only awarded at admission; Early Decision applicants receive preference. Covers eight semesters of full-time study, including Dickinson or partner off-campus study. The college's general merit policy requires good academic standing (2.0 GPA). The program requires FAFSA and CSS Profile but does not state financial need is a selection criterion.

name: Curley Scholarship
value: Two half-tuition scholarships awarded annually, for eight semesters of full-time study
deadline: Submit the complete admission application, FAFSA and CSS Profile by the admission deadline. For fall 2027 admission: Early Decision I and Early Action November 15, 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 15, 2027.
apply: No separate application. Submit a complete admission application plus the FAFSA and CSS Profile by the deadline; Early Decision applicants get preference.
eligibility: Incoming students who live or attend school in Lycoming, Lehigh or Northampton counties, Pennsylvania.
notes: Only awarded at admission; Early Decision applicants receive preference. Covers eight semesters of full-time study, including Dickinson or partner off-campus study. The college's general merit policy requires good academic standing (2.0 GPA).

name: Music Scholars Award
value: Covers one full credit of private studio lessons each semester (up to $1,500 annually or $6,000 over four years)
deadline: Submit SlideRoom materials by the admission deadline. For fall 2027 admission: Early Decision I and Early Action November 15, 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 15, 2027.
apply: Submit SlideRoom materials through the Common Application. Instrumentalists and vocalists submit two solo video performances, preferably contrasting styles; audio-only and nonsolo ensemble videos are not accepted. Composers submit PDFs of two contrasting compositions, with recordings optional. Music history, theory or ethnomusicology applicants submit a PDF writing sample, with original multimedia optional. Awards are announced with the admission decision.
eligibility: Prospective first-year students with musical talent; recipients do not need to major in music.
notes: Must join a faculty-led ensemble (Choir, Jazz Ensemble or Orchestra) and take lessons or a music course each semester.

name: Gettysburg Academic Merit Scholarships
value: For fall 2026 entrants, $30,000 to $53,000 annually, renewable for up to eight semesters. Fall 2027 amounts have not been published on the page reviewed.
deadline: No separate deadline; considered with the Common Application.
apply: Submit the Common Application; no separate scholarship application.
eligibility: All first-year applicants are considered, based on academic achievement, leadership and potential to contribute to the campus community.
notes: Awards are fixed at admission and require the individual award's cumulative GPA at each academic year end, good academic standing and progress. The reviewed pages do not list the GPA threshold for each general merit award.

name: Eisenhower Scholarship for Civic Engagement
value: $53,000 per year ($212,000 over four years of full-time study)
deadline: For fall 2027, submit both the Common Application and scholarship application by November 1, 2026 (Early Decision I), November 15, 2026 (Early Action), January 15, 2027 (Regular Decision), or January 20, 2027 (Early Decision II). Early Decision and Early Action applicants receive priority consideration.
apply: Submit the Common Application and the Fall 2027 Eisenhower Scholarship application (two 300 to 350 word essays on civic engagement).
eligibility: First-year applicants with demonstrated civic engagement, leadership and change agency in their communities.
notes: Keep with a 3.0 GPA. Non-recipients are automatically considered for other academic merit scholarships.

name: Gettysburg College-Gilder Lehrman Institute (GLI) History Scholarship
value: $50,000 per year ($200,000 over four years); a limited number awarded each year
deadline: For fall 2027, submit both the Common Application and scholarship application by November 1, 2026 (Early Decision I), November 15, 2026 (Early Action), January 15, 2027 (Regular Decision), or January 20, 2027 (Early Decision II). Early Decision and Early Action applicants receive priority consideration.
apply: Submit the Common Application and the fall 2027 GLI History Scholarship form. Write a 250 to 350 word essay on how history has influenced your values, education or engagement and inspired future impact.
eligibility: High-achieving first-year applicants with a strong interest in history shown through academics, independent research or personal experience.
notes: The fall 2027 application is available. Nonrecipients are considered for other academic merit scholarships. Renewal requires the scholarship-specific cumulative GPA and academic progress, but the reviewed pages do not specify the GLI GPA threshold.

name: Sunderman Conservatory of Music Scholarships
value: F. William Sunderman: $52,000 per year for music majors. Parker B. Wagnild: $44,000 per year for majors, minors and occasionally highly talented nonmajors. Elizabeth Headley Paul: published pages conflict between up to $8,000 and at least $8,000 annually; confirm the amount.
deadline: In-person auditions: November 9, 2026; December 12, 2026; January 23, 2027; February 6, 2027. Recorded auditions: November 7, 2026 (ED I), December 12, 2026 (EA), January 23, 2027 (ED II), February 6, 2027 (RD). Submit the Common Application by the appropriate admission deadline.
apply: Complete the Common Application, Music Profile Form and online music theory assessment. Audition in person or submit a video, then complete a faculty interview with sight-reading or sight-singing; recorded applicants interview virtually. Follow the instrument-specific repertoire requirements; jazz applicants complete both instrument and jazz requirements.
eligibility: Sunderman is for music majors; Wagnild is for music majors, minors and occasionally highly talented nonmajors. Headley Paul is described as an award for an enrolled music-degree student, with keyboard/piano preference. All require an audition.
notes: Renewal requires satisfactory music-degree progress, private study and GPA; Wagnild additionally requires faculty-assigned ensemble participation. Exact scholarship GPA thresholds are not published. Headley Paul's eligibility page says enrolled students, so do not assume it is an incoming first-year award. The separate Patrick Grant considers financial need.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: $5,000 to $40,000 per year, with larger awards to the strongest students; automatically renewed for four years of full-time study
deadline: Scholarship priority application deadline December 1, 2026. Early Decision I application November 15, 2026; documents November 20, 2026. Early Decision II and Regular Decision application January 15, 2027; documents January 20, 2027. Complete required materials by the earliest applicable deadline for priority scholarship consideration.
apply: Submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, personal essay, official transcript, counselor and teacher recommendations; testing is optional except designated combined degree programs. No separate merit application. International applicants must submit a Certification of Finances and meet applicable English-proficiency requirements.
eligibility: First-year and transfer applicants with outstanding academic and personal achievements.
notes: International applicants are eligible; binding Early Decision applicants receive preference. Funding is automatically renewed for four years of full-time undergraduate study, with a maximum of 12 Union-funded terms.

name: Henle Scholarship
value: Amount not stated; automatically renewed for four years of full-time study
deadline: Scholarship priority application deadline December 1, 2026. Early Decision I application November 15, 2026; documents November 20, 2026. Early Decision II and Regular Decision application January 15, 2027; documents January 20, 2027. Complete required materials by the earliest applicable deadline for priority scholarship consideration.
apply: Submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, personal essay, official transcript, counselor and teacher recommendations; testing is optional except designated combined degree programs. No separate merit application. International applicants must submit a Certification of Finances and meet applicable English-proficiency requirements.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students with a unique combination of outstanding talents and accomplishments, academic excellence, and promise of exceptional contribution to the College community.
notes: Established by David L. Henle. The program page does not publish a Henle award amount.

name: John F. Oberlin Scholarship
value: Amount not stated; renewable for 8 semesters (10 for Double Degree or BA+BFA students)
deadline: Fall 2027 College of Arts and Sciences admission: Early Decision I and Early Action November 1, 2026; Early Decision II January 5, 2027; Regular Decision January 15, 2027. No separate merit application deadline.
apply: Submit the Common Application or Coalition/Scoir Application, personal essay, secondary school report, transcript and one academic teacher evaluation. Early Decision requires the signed agreement; BA+BFA requires a portfolio. Additional rules apply to homeschooled and international applicants. All admitted Arts and Sciences students are automatically considered.
eligibility: Admitted students in the College of Arts and Sciences, based on academic achievement.
notes: Full-time enrollment required, except prorated funding in a senior's final semester. Academic dismissal may end eligibility. Funding does not transfer to unaffiliated study abroad or between divisions, with an exception for dual-degree students dropping one degree after year one. The separate $10,000 Commitment Scholarship goes to all enrolling students.

name: Conservatory Dean's Award
value: Amount not stated; renewable for 8 semesters (10 for Double Degree students)
deadline: Fall 2027 Conservatory: Early Decision Common Application November 1, 2026; audition/interview request, music background, recommendation requests and screening November 4, 2026. Regular Decision Common Application December 1, 2026; portal forms and screening December 4, 2026; final recorded auditions February 1, 2027. Recommender submissions December 18, 2026. Music Theater ED and early-screening applications October 15, 2026; ED on-campus audition December 5, 2026. The theory-exam instructions conflict: select-area ED applicants are told December 1, 2026, while the table says February 1, 2027.
apply: Submit the Common Application, portal audition/interview request, music background and prescreening for all areas. Request two artistic teacher recommendations, at least one from the current or latest private teacher or coach, and submit secondary transcripts and school report. Audition or interview according to the area requirements; ED requires an on-campus audition, while RD recordings are allowed except Music Theater, which requires live singing. Composition and TIMARA require supplemental essays; TIMARA and Recording Arts applicants need the theory exam for admission. CSS Profile is strongly recommended for merit consideration; FAFSA is not required for merit alone.
eligibility: Admitted Conservatory of Music students.
notes: Full-time enrollment required, except prorated final-semester funding. Academic dismissal may end eligibility; funding does not apply to unaffiliated study abroad or move between divisions, except dual-degree students dropping one degree after the first year. Music Theater has separate prescreening and live audition rules.

name: Oberlin College National Merit Scholarship
value: The award page states $2,000; the merit policy page instead states $1,000 to $2,000. Confirm the amount and payment schedule in the award offer.
deadline: Fall 2027 College of Arts and Sciences admission: Early Decision I and Early Action November 1, 2026; Early Decision II January 5, 2027; Regular Decision January 15, 2027. No separate merit application deadline. Declare Oberlin as first choice with NMSC by the competition's deadline; the 2027 first-choice deadline was not confirmed.
apply: Apply for Oberlin admission and declare Oberlin as first-choice college with NMSC after qualifying as a National Merit Finalist.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists who name Oberlin as first choice and have not won another National Merit or corporate-sponsored National Merit Scholarship.
notes: Full-time enrollment is required. Other National Merit or corporate-sponsored Merit Scholarship recipients are not eligible for the Oberlin-sponsored award.

name: USD First-Year Merit Scholarships
value: Amount not published on the current merit page; renewable for up to four years, or five years for Engineering students.
deadline: Fall 2027: Early Decision I and Early Action November 1, 2026; Early Decision II January 5, 2027; Regular Decision January 15, 2027. No separate merit application.
apply: Submit the Common Application and USD Member Questions plus required admission documents; all first-year applicants are considered automatically. USD does not consider SAT/ACT scores for fall 2027.
eligibility: All undergraduate first-year applicants to the University of San Diego (private, in San Diego; not UC San Diego), via holistic review of grades, course rigor, leadership, service, talent and personal qualities.
notes: Renewal requires a 3.0 cumulative USD GPA. Awards may combine with USD and outside aid; individual offers may include additional renewal conditions.

name: USD Music Scholarship and Choral Scholars Scholarship
value: USD Music Scholarship: $540 to $15,000. Choral Scholars Scholarship: $1,200 to $10,000.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; the Music Department says dates and more info for spring 2027 are coming soon.
apply: Audition with Music. Instrumental applicants prepare one significant work or two contrasting shorter pieces, major scales and sight-reading; percussionists prepare a mallet instrument and at least one other percussion instrument. Vocal applicants prepare two contrasting memorized selections, each no longer than five minutes, from classical/art song or musical theater; a live pianist or piano-only backing track is accepted. The spring 2027 submission process is forthcoming.
eligibility: USD Music Scholarship: incoming or continuing music majors who excel in performance, composition, education or music research. Choral Scholars: music majors or comprehensive minors.
notes: Incoming first-year music awards cover four years; transfer and continuing awards cover shorter periods. Maintain the music major except Choral Scholars, make progress toward coursework and remain in good academic standing. Choral Scholars additionally requires annual reaudition and a 3.0 GPA.

name: First-Year Merit Scholarships
value: Amounts vary; can be as high as $42,000 per year, applied to tuition only, for eight semesters.
deadline: Considered if you apply by the admission deadline. Fall 2027: Early Action and Early Decision I November 1, 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 15, 2027.
apply: Submit the Common Application and Panther Profile, official high school transcript, Common App school report and one teacher recommendation. Creative-talent majors require the applicable Creative Supplement. SAT/ACT scores are optional. No separate merit application; awards are included with admission.
eligibility: New first-year applicants, including international students, are considered without regard to financial need. Selection considers academics, curriculum rigor, application quality and test scores if submitted. Students using employee-child tuition remission or Tuition Exchange are not eligible for merit funds.
notes: Tuition-only funding for the first bachelor's degree. Renew for eight semesters with full-time enrollment (at least 12 credits) and a 2.75 cumulative Chapman GPA. Spring entrants receive half the annual amount; APEx has a shorter schedule.

name: Dodge College Talent Scholarships (Sodaro-Pankey Talent Scholarship)
value: $2,000 to $5,000 per year for four years while in good academic standing.
deadline: Considered if you apply by the admission deadline. Fall 2027: Early Action and Early Decision I November 1, 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 15, 2027.
apply: Submit Chapman's Common Application, Panther Profile and the Dodge Creative Supplement, which determines talent scholarship consideration; no separate scholarship application. Creative-talent applicants are encouraged to apply by November 1, 2026.
eligibility: Applicants to a Dodge College major showing creative ability and originality. The Dodge overview limits talent scholarships to first-year applicants, while the named Sodaro-Pankey policy also describes transfer eligibility; transfer applicants should confirm.
notes: Renew with a Dodge major, full-time enrollment of at least 12 credits and a 2.75 cumulative Chapman GPA. First-year funding is for eight semesters; the Sodaro-Pankey policy gives transfers eight semesters minus prior full-time equivalent enrollment.

name: Fowler Engineering Scholarships
value: $2,000 per year up to 100% of tuition, room and board; available for up to eight semesters.
deadline: Considered if you apply by the admission deadline. Fall 2027: Early Action and Early Decision I November 1, 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 15, 2027.
apply: Apply for admission to a Fowler undergraduate engineering major; applicants are automatically considered. Follow Chapman's Common Application, Panther Profile, transcript, school report and teacher recommendation requirements. FAFSA is required for the need-based categories. Awards appear in the Application Status Page after admission.
eligibility: First-year applicants who apply to a Fowler Engineering major. Merit awards go to students with exemplary academic records.
notes: The range includes both merit and need-based engineering awards. Renew with full-time enrollment, a STEM major in Fowler, Schmid or Crean, no Fowler course grade below B-, and at least a 3.0 cumulative Chapman GPA. First-year awards cover eight semesters; transfers receive the remainder after prior full-time equivalent enrollment. Individual offer letters specify conditions.

name: Thurgood Marshall Scholarship
value: Up to $6,000 annually toward mandatory fall and spring tuition, renewable for eight semesters for first-year students. Amounts depend on demonstrated need and may change each year; spring entrants receive half the annual award.
deadline: Complete the admission application by November 1, 2026 (EA/ED I) or January 15, 2027 (ED II/RD). Submit FAFSA by the annually published March 2 recommended financial-aid deadline for renewal; no separate scholarship application deadline is published.
apply: Submit the Common Application and Panther Profile, official high school transcript, Common App school report and one teacher recommendation. Creative-talent majors require the applicable Creative Supplement. SAT/ACT scores are optional. No separate merit application; awards are included with admission. FAFSA is required to establish and renew financial need.
eligibility: Select first-generation students with exceptional academic performance, outstanding community leadership and demonstrated financial need.
notes: Renewal requires full-time enrollment of at least 12 credits, a 2.00 cumulative GPA and annual FAFSA by the recommended March 2 deadline. Funding is for the first bachelor's degree and excludes summer and housing. Transfers receive eight semesters minus prior full-time equivalent terms; APEx follows a shorter schedule.

name: Merit Scholarships
value: $1,000 to full tuition; most are four-year awards.
deadline: December 15 priority consideration for fall applicants (displayed without a year).
apply: Submit the Hillsdale application or Common Application with writing responses, transcripts, recommendation letters and an activities resume. Test scores are optional and an interview is encouraged. No separate scholarship paperwork.
eligibility: All applicants to Hillsdale College; based on the strength of the application with emphasis on academic profile.
notes: Recipients must maintain good citizenship and moral conduct. The page says most merit awards last four years but does not publish the specific academic renewal requirements for each award.

name: Leadership Scholarships
value: Amount not stated.
deadline: November 15 for fall-term applicants (displayed without a year).
apply: Submit the Hillsdale application or Common Application with writing responses, transcripts, recommendation letters and an activities resume. Test scores are optional and an interview is encouraged. No separate scholarship paperwork. The resume should include extracurricular activities, leadership, volunteering and work experience; submit the complete application by the published November 15 deadline.
eligibility: Fall-term applicants; recognizes involvement in school, church and community.
notes: Scholarship recipients must maintain good citizenship and moral conduct. Award amount, duration and academic renewal terms are not published.

name: Choral Scholars Scholarship
value: Typically $10,000 per year, renewable according to the terms of the aid agreement.
deadline: The program home page announces choral-vocal audition days November 15-16, 2026, with no prescreen video required for participants. The detailed application page still describes fall 2026 entry with a December 15, 2025 prescreen deadline and January 30-31, 2026 auditions; a full fall 2027 application schedule is not published.
apply: For the announced November 15-16, 2026 audition days, register using the program's listed contact; attendance replaces prescreening. The older detailed process uses unlisted YouTube prescreen videos with a teacher/accompanist visible, accompanied classical or sacred solos, the assigned Mundy choral part and vocalises, followed by an invited on-campus audition. Confirm the fall 2027 submission procedure.
eligibility: Prospective Hillsdale students with singing ability and academic promise; no music major or minor is required. Awards reflect audition potential, choir voice needs, funding and applicant strength.
notes: Choral Scholars rehearse Sunday through Thursday and take part in sung services, concerts and special events. Private voice lessons may be taken without a lesson fee. Award agreements set duties and renewal terms; the current posted amount is typically $10,000 per year.

name: Honors Scholarship
value: $1,000 per year, renewable for up to four years.
deadline: Fall 2027 admission: Early Decision or Early Action I by November 1, 2026, or Early Action II by December 1, 2026. Separate Scholarship Day application by February 1, 2027. The Honors presentation date is supplied separately.
apply: Apply through the Common Application with an essay, official high-school transcript and a counselor or core-teacher recommendation; test scores are optional. Accept an Honors Program invitation and submit a project titled 'Teach Us Something in Five Minutes or Less'. Present it and answer faculty questions at Scholarship Day; international students may interview virtually if needed.
eligibility: Early Action or Early Decision applicants accepted and enrolled in the fall first-year class who are invited to and accept entry into the Honors Program.
notes: Renewal requires HONR 150 in the first fall semester and a 3.4 GPA. International students are eligible, but this award does not reduce their required financial contribution. INspire participants cannot receive additional funding above full tuition.

name: Creative Writing Scholarship
value: $2,500 per year, renewable for up to four years.
deadline: Fall 2027 admission: Early Decision or Early Action I by November 1, 2026, or Early Action II by December 1, 2026. Separate Scholarship Day application by February 1, 2027.
apply: Apply through the Common Application with an essay, official high-school transcript and a counselor or core-teacher recommendation; test scores are optional. Submit the separate Creative Writing Scholarship application and writing work in the applicant portal. Selected finalists participate in Scholarship Day; international students may interview virtually if needed.
eligibility: Early Action or Early Decision applicants accepted to the fall class who plan to major or minor in English or creative writing.
notes: Renewal requires a 2.0 GPA and either a creative writing course or at least one semester as a student editor of The Crucible. International students are eligible, but this award does not reduce their required financial contribution. INspire participants cannot receive additional funding above full tuition.

name: Music Scholarship
value: $1,000 to $2,500 per year, renewable for up to four years. The Rariden Scholarship offers $5,000 per year to select Indiana residents.
deadline: Fall 2027 admission: Early Decision or Early Action I by November 1, 2026, or Early Action II by December 1, 2026. Separate Scholarship Day application by February 1, 2027.
apply: Apply through the Common Application with an essay, official high-school transcript and a counselor or core-teacher recommendation; test scores are optional. Submit the music scholarship form, audition and an information sheet listing instruments or voice, years of study, ensemble and contest experience, composition/computer music and any piano/guitar accompanying. Prepare two contrasting pieces; voice applicants normally present a non-English classical work plus Broadway or popular repertoire. Multi-instrumentalists may use one piece per instrument. International students may audition virtually.
eligibility: Early Action or Early Decision applicants accepted to the fall class who plan to take music classes and/or ensembles; not limited to majors.
notes: Renewal requires a 2.0 GPA, one ensemble each on-campus semester and lessons each semester. Pianists may substitute equivalent accompanying work. The $5,000 annual, four-year Rariden award is for one incoming Indiana visual/performing-arts student, with Wayne County preference. International students are eligible, but this award does not reduce their required financial contribution. INspire participants cannot receive additional funding above full tuition.

name: Art Scholarship
value: $1,000 to $2,500 per year, renewable for up to four years.
deadline: Fall 2027 admission: Early Decision or Early Action I by November 1, 2026, or Early Action II by December 1, 2026. Separate Scholarship Day application by February 1, 2027.
apply: Apply through the Common Application with an essay, official high-school transcript and a counselor or core-teacher recommendation; test scores are optional. Submit the separate Art Scholarship application and portfolio. Selection considers academic achievement and the portfolio.
eligibility: Early Action or Early Decision applicants accepted to the fall class who plan to major or minor in art.
notes: Renewal requires a 2.0 GPA, an art course each on-campus semester and an art major or minor. International students are eligible, but this award does not reduce their required financial contribution. INspire participants cannot receive additional funding above full tuition.

name: Theatre Arts Scholarship
value: $1,000 to $2,500 per year, renewable for up to four years.
deadline: Fall 2027 admission: Early Decision or Early Action I by November 1, 2026, or Early Action II by December 1, 2026. Separate Scholarship Day application by February 1, 2027.
apply: Apply through the Common Application with an essay, official high-school transcript and a counselor or core-teacher recommendation; test scores are optional. Submit the separate Theatre Arts Scholarship application and audition. International students may audition virtually if needed.
eligibility: Early Action or Early Decision applicants accepted to the fall class who plan to take theatre classes and/or productions.
notes: Renewal requires a 2.0 GPA and either one departmental production plus one academic theatre course per year, or two academic theatre courses. Practicum or applied theatre credit does not count as the academic course. International students are eligible, but this award does not reduce their required financial contribution. INspire participants cannot receive additional funding above full tuition.

name: The Quaker Scholarship
value: Awards range from $5,000 to full tuition, housing and meals, renewable for up to four years.
deadline: Fall 2027 admission: Early Decision or Early Action I by November 1, 2026, or Early Action II by December 1, 2026. The specific Quaker page lists January 10 for its application and February 28, 2027 for finalist interviews, while the directory lists February 1. Confirm the earlier program-specific application date.
apply: Apply through the Common Application with an essay, official high-school transcript and a counselor or core-teacher recommendation; test scores are optional. Submit a Quaker Scholarship application with a personal reflection and verification of affiliation with a Quaker meeting or Friends school. Selected finalists interview at Scholarship Day; international students may interview virtually.
eligibility: Incoming fall students applying through Early Action or Early Decision with verified Quaker affiliation. The specific page requires Quaker meeting membership, while the directory also allows verification of Quaker faith; applicants relying on another affiliation should confirm eligibility.
notes: Renewal requires a 2.0 GPA and reasonable progress toward degree completion. International students are eligible, but this award does not reduce their required financial contribution. INspire participants cannot receive additional funding above full tuition.

name: Carleton B. Edwards Chemistry Scholarships
value: At least $1,000 per year, renewable for up to four years.
deadline: Fall 2027 admission: Early Decision or Early Action I by November 1, 2026, or Early Action II by December 1, 2026. Separate Scholarship Day application by February 1, 2027.
apply: Apply through the Common Application with an essay, official high-school transcript and a counselor or core-teacher recommendation; test scores are optional. Complete the separate Chemistry Scholarship form and personal essay explaining the planned chemistry or biochemistry major, significant experiences and any independent science study or research. Science reports or project examples are optional. The program page does not require additional scholarship reference letters.
eligibility: Outstanding incoming students who plan to major in chemistry or biochemistry; judged on high school achievement, interest in chemistry and references.
notes: Renewal requires a 2.0 GPA and reasonable progress toward a chemistry or biochemistry degree. International students are eligible, but this award does not reduce their required financial contribution. INspire participants cannot receive additional funding above full tuition.

name: Earlham Science Scholar Program
value: Up to $10,000 per year. The 2022 grant announcement described four-year support for cohorts starting in fall 2023; a new fall 2027 cohort and its award terms are unconfirmed.
deadline: No fall 2027 scholarship deadline or open application was found.
apply: Current application instructions for a new cohort could not be confirmed. Ask Earlham about availability before preparing scholarship materials.
eligibility: The original program served Pell-eligible incoming STEM students in engineering, biology, biochemistry, chemistry, computer science, earth/environmental science, mathematics, data science or physics. Eligibility for a new fall 2027 cohort is unconfirmed.
notes: The original announcement required good academic standing and offered research, conference and mentoring support. A current faculty profile still describes the grant, but it does not confirm recruitment of a new cohort.

name: Brooks Scholarship (Music)
value: Four-year, full-tuition scholarship.
deadline: 2027 Brooks application due January 15, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. EST; both music recommendations due January 22, 2027. Apply separately for admission by November 15, 2026 for ED I, or January 15, 2027 for ED II or Regular Decision.
apply: Submit a Common Application or Coalition Application with the high-school transcript and counselor and teacher recommendations; SAT/ACT scores are optional. Use the 2027 Brooks Scholarship portal for a music resume, approximately one-page personal repertoire/composition essay, and contact details for two music recommenders: current private teacher and another music teacher or professional. Performers submit two contrasting videos, no more than 15 minutes total, with accompaniment where appropriate and no editing or audio enhancement. Composers submit two original scores for contrasting instrumentations, with recordings if available.
eligibility: High school seniors who will major in music or double major in music and another discipline, with outstanding instrumental/vocal performance or composition and strong academics.
notes: AI-generated scores, including partially AI-generated scores, are prohibited. Renewal requires a strong academic record and continued active music-major participation. Holy Cross institutional scholarships are limited to eight semesters and require satisfactory academic progress; they cannot be refunded for off-campus housing.

name: Bean and FitzGerald Classics Scholarships
value: Full tuition for four years. Two Rev. Henry Bean, S.J. Scholarships each year; a Rev. William FitzGerald, S.J. Scholarship (awarded every four years) is offered this year to a member of the Class of 2031.
deadline: Admission and scholarship application due January 15, 2027; recommendation due January 22, 2027. The page gives an inconsistent January 26, 2026 interview notice and links a closed 2026 application.
apply: Submit a Common Application or Coalition Application with the high-school transcript and counselor and teacher recommendations; SAT/ACT scores are optional. Complete the additional Classics Scholarship application, two essays (600 and 500 words) and one scholarship recommender. A second recommender and AP scores are optional; selected finalists interview. The currently linked form is the closed 2026 form, so obtain the correct 2027 form before applying.
eligibility: Incoming high-school graduates planning a Classics major, with demonstrated interest in the ancient world and strong potential for academic and departmental participation.
notes: Holy Cross institutional scholarships are limited to eight semesters and require satisfactory academic progress; they cannot be refunded for off-campus housing. The department announces two Bean awards annually and the four-yearly FitzGerald award for the Class of 2031.

name: Ellis Scholarship
value: Full tuition, renewable for all four years.
deadline: Fall 2027 admission application: ED I November 15, 2026; ED II and Regular Decision January 15, 2027. The Ellis page lists finalist interviews in February without a current cycle date.
apply: Submit a Common Application or Coalition Application with the high-school transcript and counselor and teacher recommendations; SAT/ACT scores are optional. No separate Ellis application; all first-year applicants residing in Worcester are considered. Selected finalists must attend an on-campus scholarship interview.
eligibility: Worcester, Massachusetts residents entering their first year at Holy Cross.
notes: Holy Cross institutional scholarships are limited to eight semesters and require satisfactory academic progress; they cannot be refunded for off-campus housing.

name: University Merit Scholarships
value: Published range: $10,000 to $30,000, applied to tuition only. Merit awards may renew for up to eight consecutive semesters; the award-specific minimum GPA is stated in the admission award letter. The range page does not explicitly state its payment frequency.
deadline: Considered with the admission application. Posted first-year deadlines (no year shown): Early Action November 1, Early Decision I November 15, Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 15.
apply: Apply through the Common Application with the personal statement, transcript, Secondary School Report and counselor recommendation. School documents may arrive up to two weeks after the admission deadline. SAT/ACT scores and admission interviews are optional. All admitted students are automatically considered for merit aid, regardless of a financial-aid application.
eligibility: Admitted first-year students; based on overall academic record, strength of program and extracurricular involvement. No minimum grades or test scores.
notes: Merit renewal GPA varies by award and is checked after each academic year. GPA thresholds and payment schedule should be read from the individual award letter.

name: The Company Scholars
value: Full cost: tuition, room and board for four years.
deadline: Early Action November 1 or Regular Decision January 15 (no year shown); final selections by April 15.
apply: Apply to Fairfield through the Common Application with a personal statement, transcript, Secondary School Report and counselor recommendation. Request the Cristo Rey/Jesuit-school fee waiver. An initial interview is required; first-round selectees complete an additional essay and interview. Complete financial-aid documentation for the demonstrated-need component. Selected scholars have 10 days to accept and must confirm enrollment in the portal; the enrollment deposit is waived.
eligibility: High-school seniors at a Cristo Rey Network or Jesuit high school who meet Fairfield's admission profile, contribute meaningfully to their community, embody Jesuit values through character and have significant financial need.
notes: The four-year full-cost program includes tuition, room and board, mentoring and advising, research/study-abroad opportunities and an invitation to apply for the six-credit summer Academic Immersion program. University need-based aid requires full-time enrollment of at least 12 credits and satisfactory academic progress. Any additional Company-specific renewal conditions should be confirmed from the award agreement.
